body.x: Parts for electric vehicle batteries, steering sensors and smartphone connectors are thin, small and complex in shape, and they must hold tight tolerances across very large volumes.

K&E Co., Ltd., a precision press components manufacturer founded in 2014 and based in Gumi, is led by CEO Youngil Hong. At KES 2026, the company is exhibiting MDPS torque sensor components, hairpins for EV motors, precision components for EV and ESS battery cap assemblies, USB Type-C socket drawing shells and 5G RF connector drawing shields, along with PCB assemblies for automotive steering and lighting systems, smartphone camera and 3D sensing modules and the precision dies used to make the displayed press parts.

K&E works with progressive press processes including drawing, reverse drawing, forging, blanking, hemming and precision CAM forming, which let it make thin metal components with complex three-dimensional shapes and seamless structures. It also applies precision stamping and high-temperature hydrogen heat treatment to Fe-Ni alloy parts to control the magnetic properties and dimensional stability that automotive torque sensors need. Its MES records process conditions and production history by lot.

The company works with two affiliates: K&D designs and makes precision dies, and K&P provides high-density SMT, inspection, coating and functional testing. Together they support customers from product review and die development through prototyping, press production and PCB assembly.

K&E reported revenue of about KRW 10.1 billion (about USD 7.2 million) in 2025. Its USB Type-C socket drawing shell has been used in global smartphone products since 2020, with cumulative production of about 270 million units. After connecting its cleaning and heat-treatment equipment to the MES in a smart factory project, equipment utilization rose from 78.12% to 98.53% and the process defect rate fell from 2,457 ppm to 1,340 ppm. It holds IATF 16949, ISO 9001, 14001 and 45001 and SQ certification for automotive components.

K&E has no direct export record under its own name, though its products reach global smartphone makers through Korean customers' supply chains, and K&P operates a manufacturing subsidiary in Vietnam. The company's first targets are Vietnam and Mexico, and it is seeking battery component makers and Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers in the EV and ESS sectors. It plans to focus on components for prismatic battery cap assemblies, including vents and busbars, and to add die predictive maintenance and automated inspection. It says finding reliable local buyers and manufacturing partners is its main challenge, since each new customer requires custom dies, prototypes and lengthy quality evaluation.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
